recipes.title: Kao Tom (Thai Rice Porridge)
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice under cold water until water runs clear, then drain.
In a large pot, bring chicken broth to a boil over high heat.
Add rice, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice breaks down and the mixture becomes porridge-like.
While porridge simmers, slice chicken breast into thin bite-sized pieces.
Add garlic, ginger, and chicken to the pot. Cook for 8–10 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper. Stir well.
If using eggs, crack them into the porridge and gently stir to create egg ribbons.
Ladle into bowls and top with green onions, fresh cilantro, and a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Rice Pudding Breakfast
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Combine rice, coconut milk, water, palm sugar, salt, and pandan leaf (if using) in a pot.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until rice is very soft and creamy.
Remove pandan leaf. The pudding should be thick and porridge-like. Add a splash more coconut milk if too thick.
Serve warm in bowls, topped with diced fresh mango.

recipes.title: Kai Jeow (Thai Omelette)
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl. Add fish sauce, lime juice, sliced green onion, and white pepper. Beat vigorously until slightly frothy.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or skillet over high heat until the oil shimmers and is very hot.
Pour the egg mixture into the hot oil. It should puff up immediately.
Let it cook for about 1–2 minutes until the bottom is golden and the edges are set.
Flip the omelette and cook for another 1 minute until golden on both sides but still tender inside.
Slide onto a plate. Serve over steamed jasmine rice with sriracha on the side.

recipes.title: Thai Shrimp Congee
instructions: Rinse rice and drain. In a large pot, bring chicken broth to a boil.
Add rice and reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is very soft and broken down.
In a small pan, sauté garlic and ginger in a teaspoon of oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the garlic-ginger mixture and celery to the congee. Stir well.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3–4 minutes until shrimp turn pink and are cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with cilantro and extra julienned ginger.

recipes.title: Thai Sweet Black Rice Porridge with Coconut
instructions: Soak black sticky rice in water for at least 30 minutes (or overnight). Drain.
In a pot, combine soaked rice and 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is very tender and porridge-like.
Stir in half of the coconut milk, palm sugar, and salt. Cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve warm in bowls, drizzled with remaining coconut milk and topped with sliced banana.

recipes.title: Kai Toon (Thai Steamed Eggs)
instructions: Whisk eggs gently in a bowl (avoid creating too many bubbles). Mix in chicken broth, fish sauce, soy sauce, and white pepper.
Strain the egg mixture through a fine mesh sieve into a heatproof bowl or ramekins to ensure a silky smooth texture.
Place the bowls into a steamer. Cover and steam over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until the eggs are just set but still jiggly.
Remove from steamer. Top with sliced green onion and cilantro. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Kluay Buat Chi (Thai Banana in Coconut Milk)
instructions: In a saucepan, heat coconut milk with palm sugar, salt, and pandan leaf (if using) over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Add banana chunks.
Cook for 5–7 minutes until bananas are soft and tender but not mushy.
Remove pandan leaf. Serve warm in bowls with plenty of coconut milk broth.

recipes.title: Jok Moo (Thai Pork Congee)
instructions: Rinse rice and drain. In a large pot, bring chicken broth to a boil with ginger slices.
Add rice, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice completely breaks down into a thick porridge.
Season ground pork with half the soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper. Form into small meatballs (about 1-inch each).
Drop pork meatballs into the simmering congee. Cook for 8 minutes until pork is cooked through.
Crack eggs into the congee, one at a time, letting each poach for about 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, remaining soy sauce, and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls with a poached egg in each. Garnish with green onion and cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Pineapple Curry Fried Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes until pink. Push shrimp to the side of the wok.
Crack eggs into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add curry powder and stir-fry for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the cold cooked rice, breaking up any clumps. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes.
Add pineapple, red bell pepper, and raisins (if using). Toss to combine.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with green onions and cilantro. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Pad See Ew (Wide Rice Noodles with Soy Sauce)

ingredients.displayName: Wide Rice Noodles (fresh or soaked dried)
Chinese Broccoli (Gai Lan), cut into pieces

instructions: If using dried wide rice noodles, soak in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Mix dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add chicken and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until cooked through. Push to one side.
Crack eggs into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add noodles and pour the sauce mixture over them. Toss everything together, coating the noodles evenly.
Add Chinese broccoli and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the stems are tender and the noodles have slight char marks.
Season with white pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken) over Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add garlic and Thai chilies, stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add ground chicken, breaking it apart with a spatula. Cook for 4–5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil leaves, letting them wilt from the residual heat.
If desired, fry eggs sunny-side-up in a separate pan with a bit of oil.
Serve the basil chicken over steamed jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg.

recipes.title: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add diced chicken and cook for 3–4 minutes until cooked through.
Push chicken to the side. Crack eggs into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add onion and tomato. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add cold rice, breaking up any clumps. Stir-fry vigorously for 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Toss well.
Serve garnished with green onions, lime wedges, and cucumber slices.

recipes.title: Pad Thai (Nut-Free)

ingredients.displayName: Roasted Sunflower Seed Kernels (instead of peanuts)

instructions: Soak rice noodles in room temperature water for 30 minutes until pliable. Drain.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until sugar dissolves. Set pad thai sauce aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat. Cook tofu cubes until lightly golden on all sides (about 3 minutes). Remove and set aside.
Add another tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry chicken for 3 minutes, then add shrimp and cook until pink. Remove and set aside with tofu.
Add remaining oil. Stir-fry garlic and shallot for 30 seconds. Push to the side.
Crack eggs into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add the drained noodles and pad thai sauce. Toss and cook for 2–3 minutes, letting noodles absorb the sauce and become tender.
Return chicken, shrimp, and tofu to the wok. Add bean sprouts and garlic chives. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with lime wedges and a sprinkle of sunflower seed kernels if desired.

recipes.title: Larb Gai (Thai Chicken Salad)
instructions: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground chicken and break it apart. Cook for 5–6 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from heat and transfer chicken to a mixing bowl. Let cool for 2 minutes.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, chili flakes, and toasted rice powder. Toss well.
Add shallots, green onions, cilantro, and mint. Toss to combine.
Serve scooped into butter lettuce cups for a soft, refreshing wrap.

recipes.title: Pad Kee Mao (Drunken Noodles)
instructions: Soak dried wide rice noodles in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable. Drain. If using fresh noodles, separate them gently.
Mix oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over very high heat until smoking. Add garlic and chilies, stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add chicken and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until cooked.
Add bell pepper and baby corn, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add noodles and pour the sauce over them. Toss vigorously for 2–3 minutes until noodles are evenly coated and tender.
Turn off heat, fold in Thai basil leaves until just wilted. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Thai Basil Fried Rice (Khao Pad Krapow)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat. Fry eggs sunny-side-up until edges are set but yolk is runny. Set aside.
In the same wok, add remaining oil over high heat. Add garlic and chilies, stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add ground pork, breaking it apart. Cook for 4–5 minutes until browned.
Add cold rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes, pressing rice against the wok to get some char.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Toss well.
Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil leaves until wilted.
Plate the fried rice and top each serving with a fried egg.

recipes.title: Khao Man Gai (Thai Chicken and Rice)
instructions: Place chicken thighs in a pot with chicken broth, half the garlic, half the ginger, and cilantro roots. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes until chicken is very tender and cooked through. Remove chicken and reserve the broth.
Rinse rice. In a rice cooker or pot, combine rice with 2 cups of the reserved chicken broth, remaining garlic, and remaining ginger. Cook until fluffy.
For the dipping sauce: mash remaining fermented soybean paste with soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and a splash of the chicken broth.
Slice chicken thighs and arrange over the fragrant rice.
Serve with cucumber slices, fresh cilantro, dipping sauce, and a small bowl of the remaining broth as soup.

recipes.title: Rad Na (Thai Gravy Noodles)
instructions: Soak dried noodles in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain. Mix cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of cold water to make a slurry.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat. Add noodles and a splash of dark soy sauce. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until noodles have some char. Transfer to plates.
Add remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry garlic for 15 seconds, then add pork slices. Cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add Chinese broccoli and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the gravy thickens, about 1–2 minutes.
Pour the thick gravy with pork and broccoli over the charred noodles. Serve with vinegar on the side.

recipes.title: Yum Woon Sen (Thai Glass Noodle Salad)
instructions: Soak glass noodles in warm water for 5 minutes until softened. Boil for 1 minute, then drain and cut into shorter lengths with scissors.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, and minced chili to make the dressing.
In a skillet, cook ground pork over medium heat until browned and crumbly (3 minutes). Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine glass noodles, shrimp, cooked pork, shallots, celery, and tomatoes.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently until well combined.
Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Thai Crab Fried Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Crack eggs into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add cold rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes, pressing against the wok.
Gently fold in crab meat, being careful not to break up the lumps too much.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Toss gently.
Serve garnished with green onions, cilantro, and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry Noodle Bowl
instructions: Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
In a pot, heat red curry paste over medium heat for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Whisk to combine and bring to a simmer.
Add chicken slices and cook for 6–8 minutes until cooked through.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, and brown sugar.
Divide cooked noodles into bowls. Ladle the red curry broth and chicken over the noodles.
Top with bean sprouts, Thai basil, and cilantro.

recipes.title: Pad Mee Korat (Thai Stir-Fried Egg Noodles)
instructions: Cook egg noodles according to package directions until just tender. Drain and toss with a tiny bit of oil to prevent sticking.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add garlic and dried shrimp, stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add fresh shrimp and cook for 2 minutes until pink.
Push ingredients to the side. Crack eggs into the wok and scramble.
Add tomato paste, palm sugar, fish sauce, and chili flakes. Stir to combine into a sauce.
Add the cooked noodles and toss everything together for 2–3 minutes until well coated.
Garnish with green onions and serve.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Chicken and Rice
instructions: Rinse rice and drain. In a large pot, sauté garlic and ginger in a tablespoon of oil for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook for 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add rice, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 18–20 minutes until rice is fluffy and chicken is tender.
Remove lemongrass and lime leaves. Fluff rice with a fork.
Serve garnished with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Green Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Keow Wan Gai)
instructions: In a large pot or wok, heat 1/2 cup of the coconut cream (the thick part from the top of the can) over medium-high heat until it begins to separate and sizzle.
Add green curry paste and fry for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until very fragrant.
Add chicken and stir to coat in the curry paste. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, kaffir lime leaves, and bring to a gentle boil.
Add eggplant and bamboo shoots. Simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is very tender and eggplant is soft.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Adjust to taste — it should be creamy, slightly sweet, salty, and aromatic.
Turn off heat, fold in Thai basil leaves until wilted.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice, garnished with sliced red chili.

recipes.title: Green Curry with Tofu (Gaeng Keow Wan Tofu)
instructions: Heat the thick coconut cream from the top of one can in a pot over medium-high heat.
Add green curry paste and fry for 2 minutes, stirring until fragrant.
Add tofu cubes and gently stir to coat. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add eggplant, zucchini, bamboo shoots, and red bell pepper. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Season with soy sauce and palm sugar.
Fold in Thai basil leaves. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Massaman Curry (Nut-Free)
instructions: Heat the thick coconut cream from one can in a large pot over medium heat until it sizzles and separates.
Add massaman curry paste and fry for 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until deeply fragrant.
Add chicken and stir to coat in curry paste. Cook for 3 minutes until seared.
Pour in remaining coconut milk. Add potatoes, onions, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, star anise, and cardamom pods.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 35–40 minutes until potatoes are very tender and chicken is fall-apart soft.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste. Stir gently.
Remove whole spices (bay leaves, cinnamon, star anise, cardamom) before serving.
Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Panang Curry (Nut-Free with Sunflower Seed Butter)
instructions: Heat the thick coconut cream in a wok or pot over medium-high heat until it sizzles.
Add curry paste and stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add sunflower seed butter and stir until it melts into the paste, creating a thick, rich base.
Add chicken and cook for 3 minutes, coating in the paste.
Pour in remaining coconut milk. Add half the kaffir lime leaves. Simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is very tender.
Add red bell pepper and cook for 3 more minutes until softened.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. The curry should be thick, rich, and slightly sweet.
Garnish with remaining kaffir lime leaves (chiffonade) and Thai basil. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Shrimp
instructions: In a pot, heat 2 tablespoons of coconut cream over medium-high heat. Add curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add red bell pepper, snap peas, and bamboo shoots. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook for 4–5 minutes until pink and curled.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Fold in Thai basil and serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Yellow Curry
instructions: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add yellow curry paste and turmeric. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook for 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Add potatoes and carrots.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to low and simmer for 25 minutes until potatoes and carrots are very soft and tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Vegetables
instructions: Heat coconut cream in a pot over medium heat. Add curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add sweet potato cubes, pour in remaining coconut milk and vegetable broth. Add kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer for 12 minutes until sweet potato is almost tender.
Add zucchini, bell pepper, and bamboo shoots. Cook for 5 more minutes.
Stir in spinach and let it wilt. Season with soy sauce and palm sugar.
Fold in Thai basil. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry with Shrimp
instructions: Heat coconut cream in a pot over medium-high heat. Fry green curry paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add eggplant and green beans. Cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Add shrimp and cook for 4–5 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Fold in Thai basil.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Gaeng Pa (Thai Jungle Curry with Pork)
instructions: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add pork and stir for 2 minutes until coated in paste.
Pour in chicken broth (note: no coconut milk — this is a jungle curry). Add lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves.
Bring to a boil, then add green beans, bamboo shoots, baby corn, and mushrooms.
Simmer for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender and pork is cooked through.
Season with fish sauce. Add green peppercorns if using.
Fold in Thai basil. Serve as a soup-like curry, with or without rice.

recipes.title: Thai Pumpkin Curry

ingredients.displayName: Pumpkin or Kabocha Squash, peeled and cubed

instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add curry paste and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pumpkin cubes, pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Add kaffir lime leaves.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 20 minutes until pumpkin is very soft and tender.
Season with soy sauce and palm sugar.
Fold in Thai basil. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Duck
instructions: Score the skin side of duck breasts (if with skin). In a cold wok, place duck skin-side down. Render fat over medium heat for 5 minutes. Remove duck and set aside.
Using the rendered duck fat, fry curry paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return duck slices to the curry. Simmer for 15 minutes until duck is tender.
Add pineapple, cherry tomatoes, and lychee (if using). Cook for 5 more minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Fold in Thai basil.
Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Braised Chicken Thighs
instructions: Season chicken thighs with a pinch of salt and pepper. In a large pot, sear chicken skin-side down in a bit of oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until golden. Flip and sear 2 more minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and galangal. Sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and add kaffir lime leaves. Stir to deglaze the pot.
Return chicken to the pot. Add fish sauce and palm sugar.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 30–35 minutes until chicken is extremely tender and falling off the bone.
Serve chicken and coconut braising liquid over jasmine rice, garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Pla Neung Manao (Thai Steamed Fish with Lime and Chili)
instructions: Score the fish with diagonal cuts on each side. Place on a heatproof plate.
Tuck lemongrass slices into the cavity and cuts of the fish.
Steam the fish over boiling water for 15–18 minutes until flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
While the fish steams, prepare the dressing: mix lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, minced garlic, and sliced chilies. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Remove the steamed fish from the steamer. Pour the lime-chili dressing over the hot fish.
Garnish with cilantro and celery. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Thai Lemongrass Chicken
instructions: Marinate chicken thighs with minced lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, turmeric, and black pepper for at least 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook for 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Remove chicken and set aside. In the same skillet, sauté shallots for 2 minutes.
Add oyster sauce and palm sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves, creating a glaze.
Return chicken to the pan and coat with the glaze. Cook for 1 more minute.
Slice chicken and serve over jasmine rice with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Garlic Pepper Pork (Moo Tod Kratiem)
instructions: In a mortar, pound together garlic, cilantro roots, and white pepper into a rough paste.
Marinate pork slices with the garlic-pepper paste and soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork in a single layer. Cook for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Add oyster sauce and sugar. Toss to glaze the pork.
Serve over jasmine rice with any remaining pan juices drizzled over.

recipes.title: Thai Sweet Chili Glazed Salmon
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix sweet chili sauce, lime juice, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Place salmon fillets on the baking sheet. Spoon the glaze generously over each fillet.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Braised Short Ribs in Red Curry
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Season short ribs with salt and pepper.
Sear short ribs in a Dutch oven over high heat, 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add curry paste to the pot and fry for 2 minutes in the remaining fat.
Pour in coconut milk, add lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir to combine.
Return ribs to the pot, submerging them in the liquid. Add fish sauce and palm sugar.
Cover and braise in the oven for 2 hours until the meat is falling off the bone.
Remove lid, discard lemongrass and galangal. Fold in Thai basil.
Serve the tender ribs and rich curry broth over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Eggplant and Basil Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add garlic and chilies, stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add eggplant cubes and stir-fry for 5–6 minutes. Add a splash of water if needed to help the eggplant steam and soften.
Add yellow bean sauce, soy sauce, and sugar. Toss to coat.
Continue cooking for 3 minutes until eggplant is completely tender.
Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil until wilted. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Poached Fish
instructions: In a wide skillet, combine coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Season fish fillets with a pinch of salt. Gently lower them into the simmering coconut milk.
Cover and poach for 12–15 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Season the broth with fish sauce and lime juice.
Carefully transfer fish to serving bowls. Ladle the aromatic coconut broth over the fish.
Garnish with cilantro and sliced chili.

recipes.title: Thai Satay Chicken (Nut-Free with Sunflower Sauce)

ingredients.displayName: Boneless Chicken Thighs, cut into strips

instructions: Mix coconut milk (for marinade), curry powder, turmeric, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Marinate chicken strips for at least 20 minutes.
Thread chicken onto skewers (if using bamboo, soak in water first).

For the sunflower sauce: In a small pot, heat coconut milk (for sauce) with red curry paste. Stir in sunflower seed butter, tamarind paste, and lime juice. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Grill or broil chicken skewers for 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through and tender.
Serve chicken satay over jasmine rice with the sunflower dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Tofu and Spinach
instructions: Heat coconut cream in a pot. Add curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add tofu and gently cook for 3 minutes, being careful not to break the cubes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and kaffir lime leaves. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper and mushrooms. Cook for 5 more minutes until tender.
Stir in spinach and let it wilt completely.
Season with soy sauce and palm sugar. Fold in Thai basil.
Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Mango Curry with Chicken
instructions: Heat coconut cream in a pot over medium heat. Fry curry paste for 2 minutes.
Add chicken and cook for 4 minutes until browned.
Pour in remaining coconut milk. Simmer for 12 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add red bell pepper and half the mango. Cook for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice.
Fold in remaining fresh mango and Thai basil. Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Chili Basil Shrimp
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add garlic and chilies, stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add shrimp and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until pink.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar. Toss for 1 minute.
Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil until wilted.
Serve over jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Curry Mussels
instructions: In a large pot, heat a bit of oil over medium heat. Add curry paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add coconut milk, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add mussels, cover, and cook for 5–7 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until mussels open. Discard any that don't open.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Fold in Thai basil and cilantro. Serve in bowls with the fragrant coconut curry broth.

recipes.title: Thai Tamarind Glazed Fish
instructions: Mix tamarind paste, palm sugar, fish sauce, and 2 tablespoons of water in a small bowl until sugar dissolves.
Pat fish fillets dry and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook fish for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté shallots, garlic, and ginger for 2 minutes.
Pour in the tamarind sauce and simmer for 2 minutes until thickened.
Return fish to the pan and spoon the glaze over the fillets.
Serve over jasmine rice, garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Galangal Chicken Soup)

ingredients.displayName: Lemongrass Stalks, cut into 2-inch pieces and bruised

instructions: In a large pot, combine coconut milk, chicken broth, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to let the aromatics infuse the liquid.
Add chicken slices and mushrooms. Simmer for 10 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Add cherry tomatoes and crushed chilies. Cook for 2 more minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Adjust seasoning to achieve a balance of sour, salty, and sweet.
Ladle into bowls (leave galangal and lemongrass in the soup — they're not meant to be eaten). Garnish with cilantro.

recipes.title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)

ingredients.displayName: Large Shrimp, peeled and deveined (save shells)
Thai Roasted Chili Paste (Nam Prik Pao)

instructions: If desired, boil shrimp shells in chicken broth for 5 minutes to make a richer broth, then strain out the shells.
Bring the broth to a boil. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms and roasted chili paste (nam prik pao). Stir to dissolve the paste.
Add shrimp and cherry tomatoes. Cook for 3–4 minutes until shrimp are pink and curled.
Remove from heat. Add fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. The soup should be intensely sour, salty, and spicy.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Tom Kha Tofu (Vegetarian Coconut Galangal Soup)
instructions: Combine coconut milk, vegetable broth, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves in a pot. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse the aromatics.
Add mushrooms and crushed chilies. Cook for 5 minutes.
Gently add silken tofu cubes and cherry tomatoes. Heat through for 3 minutes without stirring too much to keep tofu intact.
Remove from heat. Season with soy sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Pumpkin and Coconut Soup

ingredients.displayName: Pumpkin or Butternut Squash, peeled and cubed

instructions: In a pot, heat a tablespoon of oil. Add curry paste and ginger, fry for 1 minute.
Add pumpkin cubes, vegetable broth, coconut milk, and lemongrass. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until pumpkin is very soft.
Remove lemongrass. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until silky smooth.
Season with soy sauce and lime juice.
Serve garnished with cilantro and a drizzle of coconut milk.

recipes.title: Thai Corn and Coconut Soup
instructions: Sauté garlic and ginger in a pot for 1 minute. Add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add corn, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 15 minutes until corn is very soft.
Remove lemongrass and lime leaves. Blend half the soup until smooth, then stir back into the pot for a creamy-chunky texture.
Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Serve garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Lemongrass Shrimp Soup
instructions: Bring chicken broth to a boil. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies.
Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook for 3–4 minutes until pink.
Remove from heat. Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Garnish with cilantro.

recipes.title: Tom Yum Hed (Thai Mushroom Tom Yum Soup)
instructions: Bring vegetable broth to a boil. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add roasted chili paste and stir to dissolve.
Add mushrooms and tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Remove from heat. Season with soy sauce, lime juice, and sugar.
Serve in bowls garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Sweet Potato and Lemongrass Soup
instructions: Sauté garlic and ginger in a pot for 1 minute. Add curry paste and stir for 30 seconds.
Add sweet potatoes, coconut milk, broth, and lemongrass. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until sweet potatoes are very tender.
Remove lemongrass. Blend until smooth with an immersion blender.
Season with soy sauce and lime juice. Serve garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Fish Soup
instructions: In a pot, combine coconut milk, broth, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Add fish cubes and cherry tomatoes. Cook gently for 8 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Remove from heat. Season with fish sauce and lime juice.
Serve in bowls garnished with cilantro and chili slices.

recipes.title: Thai Egg Drop Soup with Tofu
instructions: Bring chicken broth, garlic, and ginger to a boil in a pot.
Gently add silken tofu cubes. Reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
Slowly drizzle beaten eggs into the simmering broth while stirring gently to create egg ribbons.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper.
Serve garnished with green onion, cilantro, and a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipes.title: Thai Kabocha Squash Soup
instructions: In a pot, heat a bit of oil and fry curry paste for 1 minute.
Add squash, coconut milk, broth, lemongrass, and galangal. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 25 minutes until squash is extremely soft.
Remove lemongrass and galangal. Blend until velvety smooth.
Season with soy sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Serve garnished with cilantro and a swirl of coconut cream.

recipes.title: Thai Chicken and Ginger Soup
instructions: Bring chicken broth to a boil with garlic and ginger. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add whole chicken breasts and poach for 12–15 minutes until cooked through. Remove and shred with two forks.
Meanwhile, soak glass noodles in warm water for 5 minutes, then add to the broth.
Add napa cabbage and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, and white pepper.
Serve in deep bowls garnished with green onion and cilantro.

recipes.title: Ajad (Thai Cucumber Relish Salad)
instructions: In a small saucepan, heat rice vinegar, sugar, and salt until the sugar dissolves. Let cool completely.
In a bowl, combine sliced cucumber, shallot, and chili.
Pour the cooled dressing over the vegetables and toss gently.
Let sit for at least 10 minutes to marinate. Serve chilled, garnished with cilantro.

recipes.title: Perfect Thai Jasmine Rice
instructions: Place rice in a bowl and rinse under cold water 3–4 times until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Combine rice, water, and salt (if using) in a pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Bring to a boil over high heat. Immediately reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Do not open the lid during cooking or resting.
Fluff gently with a fork and serve.

recipes.title: Khao Niao (Thai Coconut Sticky Rice)
instructions: Soak sticky rice in water for at least 4 hours or overnight. Drain well.
Line a steamer basket with cheesecloth. Add the soaked rice and spread evenly.
Steam over boiling water for 20–25 minutes until rice is translucent, tender, and sticky. Flip the rice halfway through if possible.
Meanwhile, gently heat coconut milk with palm sugar and salt until sugar dissolves.
Transfer the steamed rice to a bowl. Pour the coconut milk mixture over the rice and fold gently. Cover and let absorb for 5 minutes.
Serve as a side dish or with mango for dessert.

recipes.title: Som Tum (Nut-Free Thai Green Papaya Salad)

ingredients.displayName: Green Beans, cut into 1-inch pieces and lightly blanched

instructions: In a large mortar and pestle, lightly pound garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add green beans and lightly bruise them.
Add palm sugar, lime juice, and fish sauce. Pound and mix.
Add shredded green papaya and cherry tomatoes. Use a spoon to toss and lightly bruise the papaya to absorb the dressing.
Add dried shrimp if using. Toss everything together.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with sunflower seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Thai Steamed Vegetables with Coconut Dipping Sauce
instructions: Steam broccoli, bok choy, carrots, and green beans over boiling water for 6–8 minutes until all vegetables are tender (not crunchy).
Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce: heat coconut milk with curry paste in a small saucepan, stirring until smooth.
Season the sauce with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Arrange steamed vegetables on a plate. Serve with the warm coconut dipping sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Thai Glass Noodle Salad with Lime Dressing
instructions: Soak glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes until soft. Boil briefly (1 minute), drain, and cut into shorter lengths.
In a small bowl, whisk lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, and minced chili to make the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine noodles, shallots, celery, red bell pepper, mint, and cilantro.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately or chilled.
